event: Windows open in the air above the circle: a Weaver, a Hearthkeeper, a Swordswoman.

memory.fact: The System's window opens in the air above the circle, and the whole hall can read it.
At a Naming the System opens a window in the air naming the class, large enough for a hall to read.

event: The girl with the mint leaf is named a Herbalist and cries, and Elsie claps hardest.
Elsie's name is called; she steps alone into the silver circle and shuts her eyes.
She opens them, and the window above her reads Enthraller.
The whole hall goes silent; somebody's breath catches, and every face turns to her.
She reads it twice over, to be sure she has the word right.
In the gallery a woman in a good dark coat rises and walks out.
Elsie says, Oh! That sounds like a lot of responsibility, and smiles at the priestess.
The priestess's hands are shaking; Elsie tells her it's all right, she isn't cross.
Outside on the steps, the Herbalist will not meet her eye, and the others step aside for Elsie.
On the lake wall alone, Elsie wishes her own window open and reads it.
Captivate and Tether; she says out loud, to nobody, that the names are awful.
Her eyes fill; she wipes them on her glove and decides to register anyway.
The guild hall on Brightwater Square is timber and noise under its copper roof.
At registration she gives her name; the clerk asks her class, and she tells him.
The clerk's pen stops mid-letter, and he goes up the stairs without a word.
The guildmaster comes down, grey-haired, with a swordswoman's walk, and takes her up.
In the office upstairs the guildmaster reads her the Strings Accord, clause by clause.
An Enthraller is registered and watched by a Warden, who writes down every skill she uses.
No skill on anyone who has not agreed to it, unless it saves a life.
Elsie asks if she can still be a healer of sorts; the guildmaster says they'll find out.
Elsie signs, pays the fee, and a copper tag is stamped with her name and an F.

changes.note: Elsie counts out her coins for the guild fee
Guild fee of two silver lanterns paid: 134 → 114 pips

event: The guildmaster walks her down to a charcoal-painted door off the main hall.
Inside, a young woman in a charcoal coat stands up with a black ledger.
She is Warden Corisande Vane, called Cora, and will write down every skill Elsie uses.
Cora says she goes with Elsie on all guild business, dungeons included.
Elsie thanks her for coming, as if Cora had chosen to.
Cora has no answer to that; Elsie asks her what she likes in her tea.
Cora says black, strong, one sugar, and her face goes still with surprise.
Elsie says she'll remember it.
At the party board Elsie asks a slate with room; its leader sees the Warden and says no.
A second party says it is full, with a space chalked plainly under its names.
A third simply turns its slate to the wall.
Cora stands a step behind her the whole time, ledger shut, watching.
In the Leftovers corner, a woman sits on the floor with a great axe across her knees.
She is rubbing her own name off a slate headed The Copper Hounds.
Elsie sits down on the floor beside her and asks if she can help.
Tamsin says she's a Berserker, and this morning she broke their shield-bearer's arm.
She says it's the third party to drop her, and she doesn't remember doing any of it.
Elsie says then she wants a healer standing behind her, and Tamsin laughs out loud.
Tamsin says she heard about the Hall: you're the Enthraller. Elsie says yes.
Tamsin says this corner is the Leftovers, she's Tamsin, and the axe is Margery.
Elsie sees Tamsin's knuckle wraps have come loose, and rewraps them, slow and neat.
Tamsin goes still and red to the ears, and lets her.
A pop and a puff of green smoke at the corner; a small woman in goggles waves it off.
She pins a notice at the Leftovers: Alchemist seeks party. Will not explode (mostly).
She is Ottilie Brandt, Tilly, thrown out of the Alchemists' College last week.
She apologises three times before Elsie has asked her anything.
Elsie asks what she makes; Tilly names a burn salve, a fizz, and something that smokes.
Elsie says a burn salve is just what a healer wants, and Tilly drops her chalk.
Tamsin says the guild licenses a party into a dungeon only with three or more.
Elsie looks from one to the other and says, then there are three of us.
On the last empty slate she chalks Elsie; Tamsin writes hers under, and Tilly hers last.
Cora watches the chalk and the red ears, and does not open the ledger.
Tilly asks, very fast, whether Elsie can make them feel things.
Elsie says she has never used her class on anyone, and does not mean to.
Cora says flatly that it's true: there would be a line in the ledger, and there's none.
At the F-rank notices they read: cellar rats, a lost goat in the Underbloom, moonbells.
Tamsin wants the goat, a real dungeon; Tilly goes white at the word.
Elsie sees Tilly's hands go to her vials, and says she'd like the rats first.
The rats are under the Crooked Kettle tea house; Elsie says a tea house is a good start.
At the desk the clerk writes the party down for the cellar rats, tomorrow morning.
Cora says she'll be at the Crooked Kettle at eight, and stays with them till the hall shuts.
They sit on the hall steps in the late sun while Tilly and Tamsin argue about rats.
Tamsin tells how she won Margery off a canal barge, and Elsie laughs till she cries.
At dusk the lamplighters' boats come up the canal and light the lanterns one by one.
Cora closes her ledger and says she goes off duty at the hall door.
Elsie asks what she'll write about today; Cora says she has not decided.
Elsie says she'll try to give her something good to write, and Cora goes.
At the Tipsy Heron across the canal, Elsie buys the other two their supper.

changes.note: Two tavern suppers at four pips each for Tamsin and Tilly: 114 → 106 pips
Elsie ends the chapter with 106 pips: 10 lanterns, 6 pips

event: Stew and bread; Tilly talks with her mouth full, and Tamsin eats Tilly's crusts.
Elsie says she loves them both already, and means it with her whole heart.
Tamsin chokes on a mouthful of stew; Tilly goes pink to the ends of her braids.
Elsie thinks that is what people look like when they're glad, and is glad too.
They part at the bridge: Crooked Kettle, eight, says Tamsin; Tilly will bring the fizz.
Elsie walks home along Thimble Canal under the lanterns, humming without knowing it.
In the attic she writes in her notebook: Tamsin, Tilly, and Cora, black, strong, one sugar.
She tells the plants she has a party now, and two friends, and a Warden.
She falls asleep with the round window open and the notebook on her chest.
